say: There's rot in the Flame's own household. Ilsa Hearthmourn wore our colours once. Now a cell shelters her, and the Nation must follow its threads.
Heresy does not walk the road alone. Someone feeds Ilsa Hearthmourn bread and steel and whispers. Find who, and finish it at her.
The Inquisition has names but not faces. Ask the priests who heard her cell confess, then the Paladins who patrol its roads. Then end Hearthmourn.
A cell of the faithless, and at its head a woman who once pacified for the Flame. I want her silenced. First, listen to those who have heard her.
Hearthmourn prays for the end of Okran, and others pray with her. The trail runs through the temple.
decline: The Flame has plenty of hands.
accepted: Begin with the priests. Confession leaves marks. After them, the Paladins on the roads. Find her, end her, and return to me.
Priests first, Paladins second. Say the Inquisition sent you. Then Ilsa Hearthmourn. Do not bring her back alive.
Speak to a priest of the Flame. Someone will have heard enough. Then ask the Paladins where the cell moves.
Quietly. The faithless have ears in the pews. Priest, Paladin, and then the woman herself.

say: The Inquisitor sent you? Then hear me and say nothing of it after. A woman came to confession and wept for a Flame that was not hers.
I have heard her cell in the dark, stranger, and I have kept it too long. Hearthmourn's people leave scraps of scripture turned inside out.
You carry the Inquisition's word. Good. Heretics hide in plain pews, and some of them hide in my congregation. Hearthmourn is among their names.
I confessed none of them, but I listened. They speak of Okran as a mistake. Your Inquisitor was right to worry.
after: The Paladins on the roads have seen their cell moving. Ask them where. I have said too much already.
Ask the Paladins. They see who leaves the pilgrim roads. I only hear who is afraid.
Not mine to say. The soldiers of the Flame know the ground. Speak to a Paladin.
Not mine to say. Go to the Paladins. I will pray for your errand, and for mine.

say: The Inquisition's errand? We have watched the cell move through Okran's Pride and the hills past the pilgrim roads. Hearthmourn walks with them.
Hearthmourn. Yes. We marked her camp twice and both times found only ashes. She sleeps lightly and her people are loyal.
A heretic cell hides in the open. We watch it. Ilsa Hearthmourn leads it, and she was good with a blade before she lost her faith.
You are the Inquisitor's hound? Then the cell is in the hills beyond the pilgrim roads, and the woman at its heart is yours.
reply: Then I know where to look.
She will not leave those hills.
after: Do not offer her the Flame's mercy. The Inquisition does not wait for it.
Take care. She prays while she fights. It is worse than it sounds.
Strike once and leave nothing for her cell to bury.
She is not the only one in that cell. Do not think the rest are lambs.

say: Hearthmourn is dead? Then her cell will wither. The Flame is grateful, and so is the Inquisition.
You followed the thread to its end. The Nation doesn't often thank, but it pays.
Ashes, I hear. Good. The heresy won't outlive its mouth. This is what the Inquisition owes you.
She prayed for the end of Okran and got her own. Take the Nation's coin and keep silent about the rest.
A man crawled out of a slave farm last week, half dead, with a name on his lips. The ones who got away know more than we do.
We keep hearing about a farm where they're worn down in rows. The woman who runs it's Grace. The escaped talk. Find one who will tell you.
Our network is thin and the farms are big. Find an escaped slave. They know where the keys are kept and who holds them.
There's a mistress who does her own whipping. Slave Mistress Grace. The runaways know her face. Go and listen to them.
Tips travel faster than chains. Ask the escaped about Grace, then do what we can't.
accept: I want her name on my blade.
decline: That is a bigger fight than I want.
accepted: Find an escaped slave. Any camp, any road. They will tell you where Grace works. Then end her.
Talk to the runaways first. They remember everything. When you have what you need, kill the Mistress and come to me.
The freed know the way in. We know what the farm is. You will do the rest.
Quietly with the runaways, loudly with Grace. Come back when she is dead.

say: You ask about Grace? I wore her collar. She works the rows herself and she counts every one of us. I don't sleep because of it.
Slave Mistress Grace. I know the name in my back. She keeps the farm and she keeps the whip, and she keeps the best guards for her own door.
You're with the Anti-Slavers? Then here's what I know: Grace never leaves the farm. Not for markets, not for her own sake.
I got out in the night. Grace is still in there. I hear her at night, I think. Do not let her live.
reply: Tell me how to find her.
She will not hurt anyone else.
after: Look for the Mistress in the rows of her own farm. Go in hard. They never expect the rows to fight back.
She will be at the centre of her farm, as always.
Strike at the heart of the farm. The guards fall back when she falls. They fear her more than they fear death.
Be quick. Every day she lives is a day someone does not wake up.

report.state: Slave Mistress Grace killed by player
say: Grace is dead? The farm is open? The Anti-Slavers pay what they owe. It is little for a thing this large.
You went into the rows and came out. Take the cats. The runaways will remember you.
The Mistress is gone, and the keys are loose. That's worth more than anything we can pay, but take this.
We heard it before you reached us. Slaves are singing in the camps. Here is your reward.
Tora was one of us. The Stone Golem took her horns and she kept her blade. A warrior who won't put down her sword must be answered with one.
There's a stain in the Kingdom's name. Tora, the one they call Gutless. Honour says she's met in the open, blade to blade.
You aren't Shek, /FLATSKIN/. But the Kingdom will honour a duel fought well. Tora refused her disgrace. Now she must be refused her life.
A disgraced warrior who still carries steel is a challenge to every one of us. Take it up, /FLATSKIN/. We'll remember the answer.
Tora lives, and that's a question none of us can answer in words. Answer it with a sword.
decline: Find a warrior of your own.
accepted: Speak to the warriors at the gates first. They will give you the terms. One blade, no tricks, no run.
The gate guards know the rule of the duel. Hear it from them. Then meet her. Alone.
Honour requires the terms be stated. A gate guard will state them. After that, it is you and Tora.
Go. Hear the terms. Meet her. Return when she is dead and you are not.

say: You come about Tora? Then hear the terms. One blade. No tricks. No second to flee. A duel is answered in the open.
Tora. We don't say that name inside the walls. If you fight her, fight her like a Shek, /FLATSKIN/.
The Kingdom's honour is simple. If you meet her, you meet her face to face. If you win, you're owed. If you lose, she's owed.
A duel isn't a hunt. You don't use a trap. You don't use a crowd. You walk up and you draw.
after: She will not run. She never did. That is the tragedy of her.
She keeps to the wastes. Go with a clean blade and a clear head.
If she asks your name, give it. She will want to know whom she kills.
The Stone Golem does not speak of her. We speak of her when he cannot hear.

say: Tora is dead. She met the blade as a warrior should. The Kingdom marks your name.
You fought her and you stand. The stain is washed. Take the Kingdom's coin, /FLATSKIN/.
A Shek who dies by the sword hasn't died in shame. Take this. It isn't payment.
The duel is done. She had her answer and so do we.
Boss Simion has the Rebel Farmers behind a palisade and a long list of Empire fields burned. The Cities want the head, not the farm.
Farmers are loyal until they're hungry. Simion made them hungry. Speak to the loyal ones, then end him.
Someone is burning tax-collectors and calling it justice. Boss Simion. The Empire doesn't pay for justice, but it pays for his head.
Rebellion is bad for trade. Simion has done a great deal of it. The loyal farmers know where his men are. Ask them. Then ask him.
A fort of angry peasants is still a fort. The Cities need it empty. Start with the farmers who still pay their dues.
accept: I will speak to the farmers.
accepted: Find a loyal farmer of the Empire. They will tell you what they know. Then Simion, and then me.
The farmers know the ground. Ask them. Then take the head to the Cities, or the news of it.
A farmer first. Then the fort. Come back with the Boss dead.
Do not trust a farmer you cannot see. Do trust the ones who still pay. They will tell you.

say: The Empire sent you about Simion? Aye. He takes half the harvest at the point of a blade, and calls it fairness. We pay the Empire the rest.
You want Simion? Then you want a fort, a gate and a lot of angry men. I'll tell you what I know, for what the Empire is worth.
I keep my head down and my fields in order. The Rebels burn the ones who don't join.
Boss Simion. He was a farmer once, same as me. Then he stopped farming and started taking.
after: His fort has a gate, a palisade and men who do not sleep. That is all I will swear to.
He keeps captains with him. You'll want help, or a plan, or both.
End him, and half the Rebels go home. Stay alive, and the other half goes quiet.
Tell the Empire we kept our end. Tell them the rest was Simion's doing.

say: Simion is dead? The Cities thank you and pay promptly. The fields will be quiet by autumn.
A good job. The Rebels will hold a funeral and burn nothing. The Empire is satisfied.
You ended a rebellion's head. Take the cats. Do not expect the farmers to say thanks.
The Boss is dead and the fort is leaderless. Here's the Cities' coin.
The Red Sabre boss sits in his hideout with a score of blades and takes a cut of every cart through the wet. We want him out of the mud.
Red Sabres drink our rum and rob our roads. Their boss never walks out. Someone has to walk in.
The barman hears things. Ask him about the Red Sabre hideout. Then do what we can't.
Swamp law is simple. Don't steal from your neighbours. The Red Sabres never learned it.
A boss who hides is a boss who is afraid. The Red Sabre is afraid of something.
accepted: Ask at a swamper bar. Barmen hear what the bandits boast of. Then walk in and end him.
Talk to the barman first. He will know when the boss has visitors. Then you decide.
A bartender is better than a map. Go, drink, listen. Then the Red Sabre.
Bring his sabre if you want to. We want him dead, not famous.

say: Red Sabre boss? I pour for his men when they have coin. They drink quietly and brag loudly. He stays in his hideout and sends boys to collect.
You ask the wrong man, but I hear things. The Red Sabre boss does not leave the hideout. He thinks the swamp will keep him.
A score of blades around him and a bounty on his head. Men talk.
Ask me nothing you can't pay for. The Red Sabre has a hideout, a lot of friends and a lot of mud. That's all I know.
after: Deep in the wet. You'll hear it before you see it. They are loud and they are scared.
Go in carefully. The mud hides more than footprints.
End him quickly. A man like that breeds replacements.
Tell nobody I spoke. Red Sabres drink here too.

report.state: Red Sabre Boss killed by player
say: The Red Sabre boss is dead? The wet breathes easier. Here are the swamp's cats.
Mud and blood and a bandit boss gone. Good work.
You walked into the hideout and out again. That is rare. Take the pay.
The sabres will scatter. Whoever replaces him will think twice.
The University studies Skeletons. The Elder preaches against flesh, and his followers prey on travellers. He's a data point we can no longer afford.
A Skeleton leader called the Elder gathers Skeleton Bandits to his iron hall. The University would prefer his study to end.
Our research relies on Skeletons who still speak. The Elder's creed doesn't. A Skeleton must hear the end of it.
The scholars have a bounty. An odd one: the Elder, a Skeleton, a leader. Ask the Skeletons who live in the towns. They'll tell you about him.
There's little the University pays for outside a book or a part. The Elder is both. We want him dead and his core intact.
accept: I will speak to the Skeletons.
decline: I do not fight Skeletons for books.
I have no quarrel with him.
accepted: Find a Skeleton in one of the towns. They know the Elder's creed. Then you will know where he waits.
Skeletons talk in short sentences. Ask the town ones. Then walk into the iron hall.
A resident of a Skeleton town will know. Ask. Then end him, and return with the news.
You will not find him by asking people. You will find him by asking Skeletons. Go.

say: The Elder. He says we're superior. We're free of flesh. Some Skeletons like it.
Elder. Iron hall. Many followers. He wants all Skeletons to follow. We don't all follow.
You ask about the Elder. I'm not him. I'm not his. I'll tell you what I know.
He's a danger to Skeletons who don't agree.
after: Iron headquarters. Hard walls. Many blades. Take care.
He is strong. His sabre is better than your sword. His followers will not run.
I will not help. I will not stop you. That is what I can offer.
I cannot tell you more. I can only tell you he is not wrong about everything.

say: The Elder is dead. The University is grateful and the Skeletons are quieter. Here is the pay.
You ended a creed, or at least its voice. Our scholars will study what is left. Take this.
A leader of Skeletons, ended by flesh. The irony isn't lost.
Intact or not, he's gone, and that's enough. Take what the University owes.
The Skin Bandits wear their victims. Their master, Savant, has a bounty on him the size of a small city. The Cities want him gone.
Savant. He skins the living and sits on a throne of the work. The Empire pays for his head. Ask the hunters who have tried.
Bounty hunters have gone after Savant and not returned. The Cities want someone who might. Ask them what they learned.
The Skin Bandits' king has a posted price that rises each year. I'd like to see it paid. Learn what you can first.
Savant. A name that means little and a record that means everything. End him.
accepted: Find a bounty hunter. They know the cost of failing. Then kill Savant and return to me.
Ask the hunters what they know. Then do what none of them could.
Do not go in blind. Hunters have tried and died. Listen. Then end him.
He sits on his throne among his own. Be prepared. Come back with news of his death.

say: Savant? I tracked him once. Three of mine went in and none came out. If you go, bring more than courage.
You're after the Skin Bandit king? He's half mad and fully lethal. His throne room is a place you don't forget.
Savant has a price on him. I'd take it myself if I valued my skin.
I know where his road leads. It leads to a throne and a lot of dead hunters. If you want his head, you will be next in line.
after: He sits in the Skin Bandit country. Bring armour, not clothes.
He is quick and mad, and his bandits are many. Plan for both.
Go in hard and leave nothing alive. He will not give you a second chance.
If you live, tell the Empire we tried first. It matters at the paying.

say: Savant is dead? The Cities have waited years. Here's more than a soldier earns in a lifetime.
You did what ten hunters couldn't. The Empire pays what it promised. Spend it before the next war.
The Skin Bandits have lost their king. The Empire doesn't weep.
Savant's throne is empty. That's worth a fortune, and here it is.
The Dust King holds the dry roads with more men than the Guild can field. Speak to the mercenaries who have walked them, then take the contract.
Dust Bandits answer to a king. The Guild would see the crown removed. Ask the sellswords who have walked his roads.
A king of sand and thieves. The Guild pays well for his end. Learn how far he reaches before you try.
The Dust King is a business problem. Too many caravans paid him. Too many guards died. Learn from the ones who lived.
A contract for the Dust King's crown. Nobody has finished it. Talk to the veterans first.
accept: I will talk to the veterans.
Where does the Dust King sit?
decline: That is a war, not a contract.
accepted: Find a sellsword who has been out there. They will tell you what the walls are like. Then end him.
Ask the mercenaries what they saw. Then take the contract all the way to his throne.
Listen to those who survived. That is the cheapest advice you will ever get.
Hear the veterans first. Then the Dust King. Then me.

say: Dust King? I was hired to guard a wagon on his road once. The wagon got through. I didn't like how.
The Dust King keeps a lot of men and a thick wall. Go in with less than a dozen and you stay in.
You want to kill the Dust King? Everyone does. Few have the stomach for the cleanup.
I took coin to run his road once. I took more coin not to run it a second time. Make of that what you will.
after: His men watch the dry roads. They will see you long before you see them.
He is cautious. That is why he is alive. Be quicker than his caution.
Strike when his men are away. They are away more often than you'd think.
Take a medic. Do not take a lot of pride.

say: The Dust King is dead. The Guild has waited a long time for this.
You did what a company of sellswords couldn't. The cats are yours, and the Guild's thanks.
The dry roads are open. Some other thief will fill the gap, but not this month.
Dust King down. The Guild will make a speech about it. You have the better end: the cats.
One of us left. He took seven others. They speak with seven voices and none of them are ours. This is a wound.
A drone who left the Hive isn't a drone. He's a question. We would like the question ended. Speak to the workers first.
Tchik of Seven Voices. Once of the Hive, now of nothing. The workers know where he walks.
We're many and one. He's one and many. The difference is intolerable. Speak to the workers, then to him.
A drone and seven who followed. The Hive remembers. The Hive doesn't forgive.
decline: The Hive can mend its own wounds.
accepted: The workers hear much. Listen to them. Then find Tchik and end the question.
We cannot say where he walks. We can say who might. A worker will tell you.
A worker. Then Tchik. Then us. We will pay when it is done.
He is not dangerous alone. He is dangerous with seven. Be ready.

say: He left. The Hive felt it. A cold place where a warm one was. He walks in the Dark Finger, I think, with the others.
Tchik. We do not say the rest. Seven voices, one throat. It is an ugly sound.
I saw him once, in the desert. He didn't know me. He knew the others. He spoke in all their voices.
He's lost. He's hungry. He's dangerous. I'm sorry for all of it.
reply: Is there any hope for him?
after: Desert and the Dark Finger. Where the paths split and the wind sings.
Seven, and a few more. They carry him as much as he carries them.
No hope. We would rather he be at peace.
Be gentle with him, if you can. The Hive is not gentle with itself.

report.state: Tchik of Seven Voices killed by player
say: He's quiet now. The Hive feels it. A warm place where a cold one was.
Seven voices, and now none. The Hive is grateful.
The wound is closed. It will scar.
The drone who left has returned to nothing. We're many again.
The Inquisitors are asking questions in the confessionals. Someone has been feeding a heretic.
They say there is a cell in the hills, and Hearthmourn's name is the first word in it. Do not say it loudly.
Seen a priest packing his scripture in the night. Maybe nothing. Maybe a name on the Inquisition's list.
Faith has a rot in it these days. Hearthmourn used to be one of ours. Now we hunt our own.
A Paladin told me the cell is moving. He did not say where. He did not look well.
If the Inquisition comes for you, you have already lost. If they want a hired hand instead, you have a choice.
Hearthmourn was a Pacifier. Now she is a sermon turned inside out. The Flame will not forgive her.
A priest in my district stopped sleeping. Said he heard things he cannot unhear. Then he stopped speaking at all.
The Nation loses a few every month to doubt. Better to lose them to the sword than to the whisper.
Holy Nation is hunting its own again. A woman called Hearthmourn who won't pray the way she's told.
Heard the Inquisition is paying for an old Pacifier. Funny, they never pay for anything else.
The Nation turns on itself eventually. Hearthmourn today, somebody else tomorrow.
There's a cell of the faithless out there, people say. Even the Flame can't keep everyone in line.
Hearthmourn is dead. The Inquisition has quietly stopped asking questions at the temple doors.
They burned the cell's scripture in the square. Someone put the woman's ashes in with it, they say.
The Pacifier who forgot her prayer is gone. Funny how quiet the pews are now.
Somebody took the Inquisition's coin and ended the Hearthmourn cell.
Holy Nation wiped out some heretic cell in the hills. Somebody paid for it, I heard.
The Nation's Inquisitors have one fewer name on their list.
Word is the Flame's hounds got their woman. Hearthmourn, something.
The Holy Nation is quiet about some heretic they burned. That usually means a loud one.
Runaways keep turning up with the same story. A mistress who whips her own rows and never sleeps.
There's a slave farm that eats its workers. Grace runs it. The Anti-Slavers know and they can't reach her.
Heard a runaway crying in the camp last night, saying the same name over and over.
Someone has to end the Mistress. I would, but I have a family and a head I like attached.

states: Slave Mistress Grace killed by player

say: The escaped are all talking about the same woman. Grace. They say she counts them every night.
I got out of a farm once. Not hers, thank the stars.
Ask a runaway what they fear most. Half of them will say the Mistress.
Whoever kills Grace won't need to buy a drink for a year, in the right camps.

states: Slave Mistress Grace killed by player

say: Grace has the best output of any farm in the south. Efficient.
The Mistress wants three hundred hands by month's end. I wouldn't take that contract.
Someone is asking about Slave Mistress Grace. Wrong questions. The Anti-Slavers should keep their noses out of it.
Slave traders talk about Grace the way miners talk about a deep seam. With greed and with fear.

states: Slave Mistress Grace killed by player

say: I heard Grace is dead. The farm is open and the rows are empty. Not all of them ran far.
Mistress Grace fell at her own gate. The Anti-Slavers put it about that it was a runaway's justice.
Somebody went into the rows and Grace didn't come out. Half the south is celebrating and the other half is counting losses.
A farm gone cold. A Mistress gone cold. I cannot say it hurts to see.

states: Slave Mistress Grace killed by player

say: Slave Mistress Grace is dead, they say. The farm is losing money fast.
Grace is gone. The Slave Traders will name a new mistress by the next market, and it won't be an improvement.
Somebody opened a slave farm in the south. Not for coin, I think. The Mistress didn't live.
Heard a farm in the south went quiet. Slave Traders are blaming the Anti-Slavers. The Anti-Slavers are blaming luck.

states: Slave Mistress Grace killed by player

say: Tora still carries her blade. Every Shek knows it and none of us can look away.
A warrior without horns is a warrior without a name. Yet Tora will not die quietly.
There's talk of a duel. Honour wants it settled. The Stone Golem doesn't speak of it.
Gate guards turn their heads when her name is said. Shame is a heavy thing to carry.
Shek have a disgraced warrior in the dust. Tora. She keeps her sword and her pride and nothing else.
Heard the Kingdom wants a duel. Foreigners only, of course. They wouldn't dirty their own hands.
A Shek without horns, still fighting. I wouldn't cross her road for a month's wages.
Tora the Fearless, they used to call her. Now the Kingdom calls her something else.
Tora is dead. They say it was a duel, clean. The Kingdom has gone quiet, which is its own kind of praise.
Gate guards say her name again. That's how you know it's over.
She died on a blade, in the open, like she wanted. That is more than most get.
The Kingdom didn't cheer. Shek don't cheer. But something in the walls loosened.
Tora is dead. A foreigner did it, they say, and the Shek approved. I did not think they could.
That disgraced Shek, Tora, finally fell. They say it was a fair duel. I didn't think Shek knew fair.
The wandering Shek with no horns is gone. Somebody met her sword.
A Shek duel ended well, for once. Even the Kingdom looked pleased, and that's saying something.
Rebel Farmers burned another tax-wagon last week. Boss Simion sends the ashes back with a note.
The Empire keeps asking for Simion's head. The Empire keeps not paying enough for it.
Loyal farmers pay their dues in fear now. The Rebels watch the road.
I knew a man who joined Simion. Last I saw him he had a scythe and a stolen helmet.
Boss Simion has a fort, a grudge and a lot of men. The Empire is nervous.
A peasant rebellion, they call it. Fires and dead tax-men. Hard to sell to either side.
Don't take a contract from the Empire against Simion.
Simion's captains are better armed than half the city watch. I'd stay away.
Simion is dead. The Empire declared a holiday and the farmers declared nothing at all.
The Rebel Farmers lost their Boss. Some went home. Some went further into the hills, angrier.
I heard it was a stranger, not a soldier. The Empire will still take the credit.
No more tax-wagons burning, for now. The fields are quiet and nobody trusts it.
Rebel Farmers lost their leader. Somebody killed Simion. The Empire will be insufferable.
That farmers' rebellion in the north-east went quiet. They say the Boss fell.
Simion's gone. Whoever did it got paid by the Cities. It's a living.
Fort Simion is leaderless. The Empire's tax-men are heading back out, and nobody is cheering.
Red Sabres took another cart on the south road. Their boss sits in the hideout and counts.
A score of Red Sabres around one fat man. You could tell the whole swamp where he's and it wouldn't matter.
Whoever kills the Red Sabre boss will drink free in every swamper bar. I'll pour the first one.
Red Sabres drink our rum and rob our roads. Their boss never walks out.

states: Red Sabre Boss killed by player

say: Red Sabres have a boss with a hideout somewhere in the mud. Everyone knows.
Swampers want the Red Sabre dead. They've been saying so for years.
I'd take a Red Sabre contract if the price were right. It never is.
Don't cross the swamp roads at night. Red Sabres don't care who you are.

states: Red Sabre Boss killed by player

say: The Red Sabre boss is dead. The roads through the wet are quiet, which makes the quiet itself nervous.
Somebody walked into the hideout and out again. The sabres don't know who to be afraid of.
A new Red Sabre will rise. They always do. But for now the wet can breathe.
Swampers poured one for the dead boss. Not out of love.

states: Red Sabre Boss killed by player

say: The Red Sabres lost their boss. Somebody went into the swamp and walked out again.
Heard the Red Sabre is dead. The swamp is a quieter place and a more nervous one.
Whoever killed the Red Sabre is a fool or a legend. In the swamp it's the same thing.
Red Sabres without their boss will do what bandits do: split, bicker, and rob in smaller numbers.

states: Red Sabre Boss killed by player

say: The Elder says we're free of flesh. I'm free of nothing.
Some Skeletons follow the Elder. Some don't.
Iron hall. Many followers. Many blades. I don't go there.
The Elder is loud. Loud draws attention.
The University has a question and the Elder is the answer. They don't like what it says.
A Skeleton leader who preaches against flesh, and a university of flesh that studies him.
Machinists pay well for Skeleton data. Better for a Skeleton leader's end.
The Elder's followers are no use to scholarship. They only fight. The scholars hate waste.
Skeleton Bandits have a leader called the Elder. He wants every Skeleton to join him. The rest of us just want them to go away.
Heard the Elder keeps an AI core in his hall. Whoever takes it could buy a town.
Skeletons preaching about being better than us. I've heard it before from others.
Skeleton Bandits follow a leader called the Elder. They take what they like from the road and call it freedom.
The Elder is dead. The Skeleton Bandits are a rabble now. No creed, no leader, just rust.
Machinists paid for it, I heard. Scholars with a bounty. The world is stranger than it was.
The Elder fell. His followers will break one way or the other. Skeletons don't mourn.
Somebody ended the Elder. A Skeleton remembers. A Skeleton doesn't forgive.
The Skeleton Elder is dead. The whole Skeleton Bandit crowd are leaderless now.
Somebody put down the Elder. The University paid. That's all I know.
Skeleton Bandits will be crossing the roads in smaller bands now. Be careful.
A Skeleton leader is down and the University is smug. I didn't know scholars could pay for killing.
Savant's bounty went up again. The Empire would pay anything to see that throne empty.
Bounty hunters keep going out after the Skin Bandit king. Few come back.
A noble told me Savant's price is the highest in the Empire. I told him I'd rather keep my skin.
They say Savant sits on a throne and wears his work. I don't ask for details.
Skin Bandits have a king called Savant. The nobles want him dead and nobody wants to be the one.
I'd go after Savant if the pay were ten times what it is.
A mad king on a throne, wearing his victims. I've heard worse, but not often.
The Empire's bounty on Savant is the worst-kept secret in the Ashlands.
Savant is dead. The Skin Bandits are a rabble. The Empire has paid the largest bounty in memory.
Whoever killed Savant is a rich person today. I would like to meet them. From a distance.
Savant's throne is empty. They say you could hear the Ashlands exhale.
Savant fell. Somebody finally did what the bounty hunters couldn't.
Savant, the Skin Bandit king, is dead. The Ashlands are quieter by one madman.
The Empire paid out the largest bounty ever. Somebody finally killed Savant.
I heard the Skin Bandits will scatter now. Which means they'll spread.
Whoever collected Savant's bounty has more cats than a small town. I wouldn't walk the same road.
The Dust King has the dry roads. Every guard who goes out there prices that in.
A Guild contract for the Dust King's crown. I'd take it if I had a company.
Dust Bandits bleed caravans. Their king does it politely.
Veterans of the dry road don't tell stories. They tell warnings.
The Dust King wants coin, not blood. The blood comes second, when you refuse.
I paid the Dust King once.
Whoever ends the Dust King will have the whole south asking for favours.
Dust Bandits never run out of men. They only run out of leaders.
The Dust King is dead. The Guild paid out. The dry roads are open, at least for a while.
A sellsword did it, or someone who looked like one. The Guild is taking credit.
Dust Bandits are fighting over the crown. Let them. It keeps them busy.
The Dust King died and not one caravan master wept.
The Dust King is dead. The Dust Bandits are leaderless and angry.
Heard the Mercenary Guild got its man. The Dust King. I didn't think anyone would.
A king of sand, ended by a hired blade. The south will be bandit-free for a month, maybe two.
Somebody is selling the Dust King's gear in the markets.
Tchik left. The Hive felt it. We don't speak of it, but we feel it.
A drone with seven voices. It's a wrong sound. Even the queen turns her head.
Something walks where the paths split. It's one and it's many.

Seven voices fewer in the desert. I sleep a little better.

say: Paladins are walking the hill roads in twos now, which they never do. Something has them looking over their shoulders.
Pilgrims say they saw Hearthmourn's people burning prayers in a ditch. They didn't stay to watch.
The Holy Nation has begun checking pilgrim packs for forbidden pages. Not for coin.
If you wear Flame colours and the Inquisition stops you, answer fast and look afraid. It's the only safe answer.
A priest said a name in the confessional once and a Paladin turned up that night. Be careful what you whisper.
The old priests are listening harder than they used to. Some say they sell what they hear to the Inquisition.
I used to trust my confessor. Now I confess in the dark and in a whisper, and mostly to myself.
The Inquisitors only visit a town when something is wrong. They have visited more towns this year than the last three.
Runaways are turning up at the waystations with raw wrists and one name. The Anti-Slavers are listening, for once.
A slave trader told me the south farm is short of hands. Short of living ones, he meant.
I buy from the farms. I don't ask who runs them. That's how I sleep.
A girl crossed the dust last week with no collar and no shoes. She wouldn't say where she came from. She only said the name Grace.

states: Slave Mistress Grace killed by player

say: Free men do not know what the Mistress does at night. I do. Ask me nothing. I will tell you anyway.
The Anti-Slavers pay for names. Grace is the biggest name I know. Do you have a blade?
I counted the rows. I counted forty before they caught me counting. Grace didn't smile.
I got out. Thirty didn't. Grace remembers every one of us, and I remember her.

say: At the gate they say a duel is a gift: the one you kill takes your shame with her. Foreigners never understand.
Honour does not need a crowd. It needs a blade, a challenge, and the courage to stand where you said you would.
A warrior fights because it's the only honest thing she can do. Remember that when you meet one.
Gate duty is long. We tell stories of the duels we didn't fight. They're always better than the ones we did.
Horns are not just bone. They are what separates a Shek from a beast. Tora knows what she lost.
A Shek who kills a Shek is a stain. A foreigner who does it's a mercy, they say, though not aloud.
The Stone Golem does not speak of the disgraced. But he keeps count.
Every Shek has a story of a disgraced warrior who wouldn't die. Tora's is the only one that's still being told.
I farm the Empire's field, I pay the Empire's tax, and I sleep with a hoe by my bed. The Rebels don't ask which side you're on.
Simion was a farmer once. He sold his hoe for a sword and called it freedom. The sword is the only thing he hasn't sold.
Tax men come at harvest and Rebels come at night. Between them there's nothing left to eat.
A man in my village joined the Rebels. We buried what they sent back. It was small.
The Empire is hiring guards for the tax wagons. Double pay, people say.
Rebel Farmers don't hold land. They hold grudges. It makes them hard to starve out.
I heard the Boss has captains who were soldiers once. That's a bad sign for the Empire's recruiting.
Whenever the Empire raises taxes, the Rebels grow. The Empire never learns.
The barman at the swamp bars hears more than the Red Sabres think. He says nothing. For a price he says everything.
Red Sabres drink in the swamp towns on their boss's coin. Strange coin.
Mind what you say in a swamper bar. Half the men at the tables are Red Sabres off the clock.
I don't pour for Red Sabres on credit. I learned that the same way I learned most things: the hard way.

states: Red Sabre Boss killed by player

say: In the wet, a rumour travels faster than a man. The Red Sabre boss has been rumoured dead twice and wrong both times.
The Red Sabres paint their blades red. That's the whole joke. They aren't good at jokes.
A boss who stays in his hideout sends his boys to do the dying. A smart boss.
Swamp roads are wet in summer and wetter in blood. Take the long way round if you can.

say: Elder says flesh is a cage. I say cages have walls. I have walls.

Finch has a theory about the Elder. The University doesn't publish it. That should tell you what it says.
Iyo keeps a list of things the University will pay for. The Elder isn't the first on it, but he's the loudest.
Scholars hate waste. A Skeleton leader who preaches against study is both waste and an insult.
The University doesn't usually pay for killing. It's a sign of something that it does now.
I took a contract on Savant once. I got as far as the first wall.
Bounty hunters who go after Savant take their shadows with them, in case they need company on the way back.
A price this high is a warning, not an invitation.
Savant skins the living and sits on his work. The hunters tell it as a joke, and nobody laughs.
The Lords of the Empire argue over who pays Savant's bounty. They argue longer than he has been alive.
A noble told me Savant is a symptom of the Ashlands. I told him the Ashlands are a symptom of the Empire.
If the Skin Bandits knew the Cities would pay a fortune for their king, they'd sell him themselves.
Savant's bounty is the largest in the Empire. The nobles have stopped bragging about it.
The Guild wants the Dust King removed. The Guild wants everything removed. It only pays when someone else does the removing.
A veteran of the dry road told me the Dust King's men all wear the same boots. It's a small thing to notice.
I took Dust coin once and it bought me three days of peace. It was the cheapest peace I ever had.
Sellswords talk about the Dust King the way sailors talk about a reef. Everyone knows where it is.
A king in the dust wants a toll and a bow. A dead king wants nothing. The south is waiting on the second.
The Dust King answers to nobody. His men answer to him, and to the sun.
Dust Bandits never run out of men, so I hear. They only run out of luck.
If you pay the Dust King, you live. If you pay him twice, you live well. If you refuse, ask the sand.
